indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.3.1.1 Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicator.objective: Explain the functions of organs in the excretory system of humans

skills.description: Name the main organs of the excretory system: kidneys, lungs, skin, liver.
State the function of the kidneys (remove urea and excess water as urine).
State the function of the lungs in excretion (remove carbon dioxide and water vapour).
State the function of the skin in excretion (remove sweat, salt and water).
Match an excretory organ to its excretory product.
Explain why excretion is important for the body.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: The kidneys are part of the digestive system.
The skin does not excrete waste.
The lungs only take in oxygen; they do not remove waste.
Excretion is the same as digestion.

questions.stem: Which organ is part of the excretory system?
hints: They filter blood to make urine.
questions.explanation: The kidneys are part of the excretory system.
questions.misconception: The kidneys are part of the digestive system.

questions.stem: Which set lists organs of the excretory system?
hints: Think about organs that remove waste products.
questions.explanation: The main organs of the excretory system are the kidneys, lungs, skin and liver.
questions.misconception: The stomach is part of the excretory system.

questions.stem: Name two organs of the excretory system.
questions.explanation: The excretory system includes the kidneys, lungs, skin and liver.
questions.misconception: Only the kidneys excrete waste.

questions.stem: Which organ is NOT part of the excretory system?
hints: The stomach is part of digestion.
It does not remove waste from the body.
questions.explanation: The stomach is part of the digestive system, not the excretory system.
questions.misconception: The stomach is part of the excretory system.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the kidneys?
options: To remove urea and excess water as urine
questions.explanation: The kidneys remove urea and excess water from the blood and form urine.
questions.misconception: The kidneys digest food.

questions.stem: The kidneys produce which excretory product?
hints: It is passed out of the body.
questions.explanation: The kidneys produce urine, which contains urea and excess water.
questions.misconception: The kidneys produce sweat.

questions.stem: What do the kidneys remove from the blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys remove urea and excess water from the blood, forming urine.
questions.misconception: The kidneys remove food.

questions.stem: A person's kidneys are not working well. What is likely to happen?
options: Waste products build up in the blood
The person will digest food faster
hints: If they fail, waste stays in the blood.
questions.explanation: If the kidneys are not working well, waste products like urea build up in the blood, which is dangerous.
questions.misconception: Kidney failure has no effect on the body.

questions.stem: What waste product do the lungs remove from the body?
questions.explanation: The lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour from the body when we breathe out.
questions.misconception: The lungs only take in oxygen.

questions.stem: How do the lungs help in excretion?
answer: they remove carbon dioxide and water vapour when we breathe out
they remove carbon dioxide from the body
they get rid of carbon dioxide and water vapour
hints: What gas is in exhaled air?
questions.explanation: The lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour from the body during exhalation.
questions.misconception: The lungs do not remove waste.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'The lungs are not part of the excretory system because they help us breathe.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, the lungs are not part of excretion
No, the lungs are excretory organs because they remove carbon dioxide and water vapour
No, the lungs only take in oxygen
No, the lungs are part of digestion
questions.explanation: The lungs are excretory organs because they remove waste products (carbon dioxide and water vapour) from the body.
questions.misconception: The lungs are not excretory organs.

questions.stem: What waste products does the skin remove?
hints: You sweat when you are hot.
questions.explanation: The skin removes sweat, which contains salt and water, through the sweat glands.
questions.misconception: The skin does not excrete waste.

questions.stem: How does the skin help in excretion?
answer: it removes sweat, salt and water through the sweat glands
it gets rid of sweat and salt
questions.explanation: The skin helps in excretion by removing sweat, which contains salt and water, through the sweat glands.
questions.misconception: The skin does not help in excretion.

questions.stem: Why is sweating considered an excretory process?
options: Because sweat contains waste products like salt and water
Because sweat cools the body only
Because sweat makes the skin dirty
hints: Sweat contains salt and other waste.
questions.explanation: Sweating is an excretory process because sweat contains waste products such as salt and water that the body needs to remove.
questions.misconception: Sweating is not excretion.

questions.stem: Which organ matches the excretory product 'urine'?
hints: Urine is made by filtering blood.
questions.explanation: The kidneys produce urine.
questions.misconception: The skin produces urine.

questions.stem: Match the organ to its excretory product: kidneys, lungs, skin.
answer: kidneys - urine; lungs - carbon dioxide; skin - sweat
kidneys: urine, lungs: carbon dioxide, skin: sweat
kidneys produce urine, lungs remove carbon dioxide, skin removes sweat
hints: Think about what each organ removes.
Kidneys make urine; lungs remove gas; skin sweats.
questions.explanation: Kidneys produce urine, lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour, and skin removes sweat.
questions.misconception: All organs produce the same product.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches an excretory organ to its product?
hints: Skin produces sweat; kidneys produce urine.
questions.explanation: The lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour. Kidneys produce urine, and skin produces sweat.
questions.misconception: Lungs produce urine.

questions.stem: Why is excretion important for the body?
options: It removes waste products that can harm the body
It helps the body grow taller
It helps the body digest food
hints: The body needs to get rid of them.
questions.explanation: Excretion is important because it removes waste products that could harm the body if they build up.
questions.misconception: Excretion is not important.

questions.stem: Explain why excretion is important for the body.
answer: it removes waste products that can harm the body
it gets rid of harmful waste products
waste products must be removed to keep the body healthy
hints: Think about what happens if waste stays in the body.
questions.explanation: Excretion is important because it removes harmful waste products from the body, keeping it healthy.
questions.misconception: Excretion is the same as digestion.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Excretion is the same as digestion.' What is the best correction?
options: No, digestion breaks down food, while excretion removes waste products
No, excretion breaks down food, while digestion removes waste
No, both are the same process in the body
questions.explanation: Excretion is different from digestion. Digestion breaks down food into nutrients, while excretion removes waste products from the body.
questions.misconception: Excretion is the same as digestion.
